text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's cash-strapped government is investigating allegations of fraud at Harare's University of Zimbabwe, including charges that state grants worth millions of dollars were "paid out to thousands of non-existent ghost students" over the past few years. Higher Education Minister Ignatius Chombo said the law would take it course.

- The Zimbabwe government has no plans to increase its 20,000-strong police force, until it has met some of the housing and transport needs of the current force, Home (Interior) Minister Dumiso Dabengwa told the Herald. He said the present ratio of one policemen for 550 people "was not too bad".
